notes.title: Rise and Shine
notes.notes:
...although we have rather been sleeping on the job, haven't we? It's been a while. Our deepest apologies on that front: both myself and Ross have been dealing with some incredibly challenging obstacles in our lives, and it has unfortunately meant that we had to place the comic on a temporary hiatus. We realise we should’ve signaled this earlier, but events unfolded quickly. Still, it’s no excuse for having kept you in the dark.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/b23c05d2bdf9e29241518a267cdf7070d90c6036.png[/img]

I suppose the most pertinent question is: are we back? Barring catastrophe, we will be returning to production on Chapter 9 this autumn. A Place in the West—to the horror of some, we’re sure—won’t ever die. It’s just a question of when we’ll reach the end. We've published 8 chapters so far, and there's going to be 15 in total. We have every intention of concluding the story.

Thank you so much for sticking with us. It means the world. Every chapter has been discounted for the Summer Sale, so now might be a great time to jump in.

We have a surprise coming in October, but more on that later …

In the meantime, thank you. We’ll see you up ahead.

notes.title: Steam Winter Sale and 2023 Update!
notes.notes:
Hey gang!

First things first: we're sorry for the radio silence these past few months. We know you've had lots of questions on achievements - like, when will they work? - and when you can expect the next chapter, but we've had to dial our production schedule back. Unfortunately I've been really, really sick, and Ross and I decided the next thing to do was for me to focus on getting better. I'm still going through that process, but we have every intention of upping our game in 2023. And yes, that includes fixing Steam achievements and getting the comic Deck verified. These are our priorities outside of making more issues.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/7adb9e9ea7c187398d4af71f3259c28374597a11.png[/img]

Right now, though, it's the Steam Winter Sale, and we've discounted every chapter! Although the year has been slow, we're super pleased with our release of Chapter 8 - Remnant, which we honestly think is our best chapter yet. If you haven't checked it out yet, it's on sale right now.

We hope you've all had a wonderful year and wish you the very best for the next one. Merry Christmas, too, ya filthy animals.

Mike and Ross

notes.title: Interlude 7.5 - Castle Okno Released!
notes.notes:
Hey all,

We’re very proud to announce the release of [i]Interlude 7.5 – Castle Okno[/i]! It’s eight pages in length and, as is our custom with the interludes, totally free: just boot up the app or check your Steam directory for the PDF.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/65ec577307a5915ee03c891ff0c08580460081a0.jpg[/img]

[h3]What’s it about?[/h3]

[i]Over a year before Leyla and Dreyfus arrive in North America, they infiltrate a Combine weather station in Eastern Europe - Castle Okno - on a secret mission.[/i]

It’s brought to you by Ross Joseph Gardner, Michael Pelletier, Kristian Rossi, Ester Salguero, and DC Hopkins.

[h3]What’s up next? [/h3]

Well, that'd be [i]Chapter 8 - Remnant[/i]. Unfortunately the ongoing pandemic has contributed to our efforts being slowed somewhat, but we're excited to kick into gear with it in the new year. [i]Chapter 8[/i] contains some big revelations. 

We will also have more changes coming! We're going to prioritize reworking the images and PDFs to be a higher quality without hopefully cutting into file size too much. Special thanks to monad for his continued assistance in that regard. Russian translations are still in the works, but we have no update on that front. Separately, our friend Artur Neufeld has also been working tirelessly on a German translation! He has the first 4.5 chapters translated, but there's still a little bit left to do on them before release. Here's an early sneak peek. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/a4ae42bbfa4545c0efdc36842ee55a3cc5016e07.png[/img]

In the meantime, check out 7.5 and tell us what you think! Speak soon.

Mike and Ross

notes.title: Anniversary Sale and Update!
notes.notes:
Hello gang,

We hope you’ve had a stellar summer. As we head into autumn, we thought we’d give you an update on where we’re at and what to expect for the rest of the year.

We want to first take a moment to celebrate our five year anniversary of being on Steam! It's a huge milestone for us - Five years ago, Ross and I were huddled around a laptop together in Boston, pushing out the first build of the app, and preparing for the Steam Dev Days conference in Seattle. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/5b215b43ec65c62573d820d3fbdd3730a5e19d3f.png[/img]

A whole lot has changed in the world since then, and that’s true of us, too. Five chapters, two remakes, several interludes – it’s a [i]lot[/i] of pages, and puts us squarely at the halfway point in our story. We’d prefer not to take another five years wrapping things up, but comics are an expensive business.

Which brings us to the remainder of 2021. Whilst our original plan was to have [i]Chapter 8: Remnant[/i] well into production by now, it sadly wasn’t an affordable prospect. At present, [i]Interlude 7.5: Castle Okno[/i] is partway through its production cycle, and will be released before the end of the year, with [i]Remnant[/i] firing up in early 2022.

In accordance with the big anniversary, we’ve discounted all chapters and both volumes of the soundtrack by a whopping 75%. The sale will run for the duration of the day, so if you haven’t checked out the later chapters, now is a great time to do so!

We’ll see you in a few weeks. Thanks for sticking with us!

Mike and Ross

The Steam Summer Sale is now live, which means chapters 2 through to 6, plus both soundtracks, are now sale! We hope you’ll take this opportunity to pick up any chapters you’ve yet to read. We're officially halfway through our story!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/8c4676f009ef55835efd98b8d4a439319edacee4.png[/img]

It’s a flashback to Leyla’s time in Eastern Europe, and takes us to a Combine weather station somewhere in the outlands… We’ll have more details very soon. 

We are also still working on getting the Achievements fixed, and would like to apologize once again for the length of time that it is taking. Our friends Vsevolod Stepanov and Pavel Lapinsky are also hard at work on the Russian translations.

In the meantime, do pick up the other chapters – whether it’s for yourself, your significant other, your folks, your cat, your dog, whoever or whatever. Literally anyone.

Thanks for reading.

Mike and Ross

notes.title: Chapter 7 Released!
notes.notes:
Hey folks!

We’re very pleased to announce that [i]Chapter 7: The Dark Between the Stars[/i] has been released. It marks the halfway point in our story and features 38 pages of all-new artwork by Kristian Rossi, Ester Salguero, and DC Hopkins.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/45459fa073332b225ea02924fb54bf033c41cb4d.png[/img]

It’s an incredibly exciting chapter that sees the comic’s setting, New Franklin, descend into civil war as Long, Rajani, and Banks fight for control of its future.

Next up is [i]Interlude 7.5: Castle Okno[/i], which will be released for free later this year. It’s a flashback to Leyla’s time in Eastern Europe, and takes us to a Combine portal monitoring station somewhere in the wilderness…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/c731b2897c6438dfec0c7c5e0fbb739aff404d70.png[/img]

But that’s not all we’re working on. We know the wait between chapters is long. It’s not ideal, but comics are incredibly expensive and are funded by our jobs. We can only make what we can afford. However, we want to introduce more content that expands the comic’s world and gives our readers something to enjoy in those months when we’re in production.

First up is a prequel novel written by Ross. It’s called [i]Half-Life: Phase Transition[/i] and takes place a few years before the events of [i]A Place in the West[/i]. The story follows a helicopter pilot called Ray who is shipped to Eastern Europe in the first weeks of the Combine occupation, where he meets a young Leyla Poirier and joins her on a journey into the heart of City 17. We’ll start releasing it for free, one chapter a week, towards the end of the year.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/896a746dff5c7011332d5eee85787f1df1d0b547.png[/img]

Secondly we’re putting a third soundtrack volume into production. It will once again come courtesy of the very talented Chris Jolley, whose work you can check out [url=https://twitter.com/ManhattenSynth]here[/url]. The third volume comes with a twist: it will feature a narrative component, exploring the life of a particular set of people in New Franklin.

We’re very excited about all of these projects and the comic’s future – it’s going to be an exciting and surprising year! As ever, please do share news of the comic, leave us a review, and check us on [url=https://twitter.com/halflifecomic]Twitter[/url] and [url=https://discord.gg/eWJWtJEFZg]Discord[/url].

Mike and Ross

PS: In case you missed it, we have Achievements currently disabled. You can read more about this in our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/466270/view/3015701868635841707]news post[/url] from yesterday. We hope to have this resolved soon!

notes.title: Achievements Currently Disabled
notes.notes:
Hi all,

We wanted to give a quick update because we know a few people have been having trouble unlocking achievements over the last couple of months. Unfortunately, there appears to be some kind of problem with the library that we’re using where it sometimes(?) can’t seem to load the proper files.

We're incredibly sorry that this has occurred. We know it's not acceptable, especially when half of those achievements are locked behind a paywall; we're meant to deliver the service we say we are, but right now we can't. That's just not okay, and we're going to try and make it up to our readers as soon as we can.

Our plan is to hopefully work with the creators of the library to get this sorted out, but in the meantime, to keep the potential break from negatively affecting other functionality, we’ve disabled achievements within the app. In the interest of transparency, we’ll also be posting this message on the discussion forums, and adding a disclaimer to the store page. 

We will keep you updated as we continue to try and get this sorted out, and thank you for your patience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/c5f62944e2e9cbe113a8217ef3dccb6d74e5f847.png[/img]

In better news, we're not letting this set-back stop us. As much as we wanted to have this resolved before release, we don't think delaying [i]Chapter 7 [/i]is the right solution, so we're going to be going ahead with it. How soon? [i]Chapter 7[/i], [i]The Dark Between the Stars[/i], will be released both on the app and as a PDF tomorrow! If you haven't wishlisted it already, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1624290/HalfLife_A_Place_in_the_West__Chapter_7/]you can do so right here[/url]. Please do let us know what you think of it.

Best,
Mike and Ross

notes.title: Production on Chapter 7 is complete!
notes.notes:
Hey gang,

A short update carrying some very, very good news: production on [i]Chapter 7: The Dark Between the Stars[/i] has been completed! We don’t have a precise release date yet, but our plan is to have it to all of you by the end of this month. 

We’re so excited with the completed product and it represents the halfway point in our story. Better yet, it’s 38 pages as opposed to the traditional 30, and at the same price – a thank you from us for your patience over the last year of remakes!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/45459fa073332b225ea02924fb54bf033c41cb4d.png[/img]

Here’s the synopsis:

[i]The Dark Between the Stars is the seventh chapter in the Half-Life: A Place in the West saga, and continues the story of New Franklin – an American enclave with a mysterious cosmic tower at its heart.[/i]

[i]Leonard Banks, the power plant foreman, issues an ultimatum to Cormac Long and Sejal Rajani: relinquish control of the city or he will start deactivating its defences.[/i]

[i]When neither Long nor Rajani submit to his demands, Banks makes good on his threat, unleashing hordes of antlions on the city's borders.[/i]

[i]As Long scrambles to defend the breach, Rajani sees one last chance to capture Long and assume control of the city, and rallies the Opposition for an all-out assault on City Hall.[/i]

We’ll see you in just a few weeks! And don't forget to join us on our new [url=https://discord.gg/eWJWtJEFZg]Discord server[/url] and follow us on [url=https://twitter.com/halflifecomic]Twitter[/url] for more updates!

Mike and Ross

notes.title: Chapter 7 Update (and a new Discord server!)

Hey gang,

We just thought we’d give you a quick update since it has been a bit. 

We’re about to hit the halfway mark on [i]Chapter 7: The Dark Between the Stars[/i], which puts us in a comfortable position to release sometime in June. At 38 pages it’s a larger chapter than most, but that’s befitting the scope of the story. It puts us at the midway point in our comic, so it’s a big deal for us! We’re very excited as to how it’s coming together and the team are doing a stellar job.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/25c6825a0fcfeeff084d06861da4c56686d7b80b.png[/img]

We have also launched a Discord server for the comic. If you’d like to chat to us, tell us what we’re doing wrong, or have suggestions for the app, come on over! We’d love to hear what you have to say. Beyond that, you’ll find a very pleasant and amiable community of [i]Half-Life[/i] fans.

[url=https://discord.gg/eWJWtJEFZg]Join our Discord![/url]

That’s it from us for the time being. We hope you’ve enjoyed the remakes and are looking forward to the future of [i]A Place in the West[/i]. There are some big surprises in store…

Mike and Ross

notes.title: 2020 Comes to a Close
notes.notes:
Hey folks,

It’s time to ring in the end of the year. And what a year it has been. For us, it saw the completion of our plans to remake [i]Chapters 1[/i] and [i]2[/i] of our comic, which we successfully released last week. It was an enormous relief, and we’re very excited to start making some real headway on our story, starting with [i]Chapter 7: The Dark Between the Stars[/i].

Progress on [i]7[/i] is already underway and is slated for a Spring release. It’s the halfway point in our story which sees the battle between Long, Rajani and Banks reach its dramatic and explosive conclusion. Here’s a small taster of what’s to come:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/4b36bf65cd964b6d2ce8319106b649a6a8a7aefd.jpg[/img]

Following up from last week's release, we also have some things we're working on behind the scenes. The Soundtracks have been converted into being actual Soundtracks, and will be made available within the app again. We're also having a chat in the discussion boards about the image quality & compression, feel free to drop by there and weigh in if you have any thoughts on it! We'll be making tweaks there shortly. 

Finally, we're also aware of an error that occurs when launching through Steam on Ubuntu (note that the app does work when launched from the folder, and that there are PDFs available). I'm going to be getting one of my machines set up with Ubuntu so I can properly diagnose & fix that.

In the meantime, the Steam Winter Sale has just started, and we’ve discounted every chapter including both volumes of the soundtrack. It's a better time than ever to get into the comic if you haven't before. And if you have, gift it to someone you like. Thank you for your support throughout the year, and we’ll see you in 2021.

Mike and Ross

notes.title: Remakes of Chapters 1 and 2 released - and more!
notes.notes:
Hey gang,

We’re extremely excited to announce that the remakes of [i]Chapters 1[/i] and [i]2[/i] have finally arrived! This release features many things, not the least of which is [i]Chapter 1: Following Portents, Interlude 1.5: The Vortessence, Chapter 2: A Very Modern Major General[/i], and [i]Interlude 2.5: The Hand of Destiny (is charred)[/i]. 

The new chapters can be read by using our app through Steam, or by viewing the PDFs in your Steam → Steam Apps → Common → Half-Life A Place in the West folder. The original versions of these chapters can also still be accessed via the app. If you have already purchased Chapter 2, you’ll receive the new version for free, and if you haven’t, then when you do purchase it you’ll receive both versions. Chapter 1 and the other interludes are, of course, as free as they ever were.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/9ecc621eef56336cc75c3f7a343296cb93913f46.png[/img]

OH, IT’S HAPPENING, KEMP. IT’S ALL HAPPENING. 

So, that would in itself be enough for celebration, right? But we’re not stopping there. We’ve also added covers and new pages to all of the existing interludes - typically just one or two here and there that expand on the story.  Still not enough? Alright.

We’ve [b][i]also[/i][/b] included [i]Interlude 6.5: The Enemy in the Clouds[/i] as part of this release, which should help tide things over until the next chapter. It’s a curious interlude, pulling back the veil on the cosmic nature of our story:

[i]"Close to a century prior to the Black Mesa Incident, two mysterious operatives are dispatched to an experimental Combine science station on a distant world to complete a secret mission. There they discover a hidden transmission that leads deep into the heart of the Combine regime, one which hints at an insidious plot to transform the very fabric of all reality…”[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/430f22b7cc6e34bafc86553259714b9391fc8e2b.png[/img]

And finally, we’ve also rebuilt the app. We’ll leave you to discover some of the new features on your own, but in short it moves away from the Source-style menus and adopts more of its own identity. It finally has a two-page spread view, as well as support for Mac Catalina, and should in general be a lot smaller and more performant. (We’ve also [b][url=https://www.aplaceinthewest.net/]relaunched our website[/url][/b] for anyone who checks those things.)

With well over 100 new pages, this is by far our largest release to date. 

The only bad news is that  we’ve temporarily dropped support for the Russian translations. We’re working on getting everything over to Vsevolod Stepanov and Pavel Lapinsky but there’s simply so much new content that it will likely take some time for them to get through. 

But let me follow that up with more good news - [i]Chapter 7: The Dark Between the Stars[/i] is already in production! It will be 38 pages as opposed to the usual 30 (at no extra cost) and should be released sometime around March/April (but don’t quote me on that). It raises the stakes quite a bit as we enter into the halfway point of the story.

We just want to express once more how grateful we are for your patience as we spent this year correcting our past mistakes. We weren’t really sure what the reception would be, and now that the release is out, we hope you agree with us that it was the right decision. It’s all forward from here.

We hope you’re excited about what’s to come. We certainly are.

Mike and Ross

notes.title: Celebrating our Anniversary
notes.notes:
Hey gang!

Today is our anniversary. It’s been exactly four years since we launched on Steam. Where that time’s gone we can’t quite say for sure, but we think we’ve used it well: six chapters, not including the remakes, and several interludes, bringing us just shy of the halfway mark in [i]A Place in the West[/i]’s story.

It’s a lot of content, and we couldn’t be prouder of our team, past and present: Kristian Rossi, Ester Salguero, DC Hopkins, and formerly Javier Puga, Ivan Miranda, Heath Heil, and Rachel Deering. We’re so privileged to work with such phenomenally talented people, and each of them, in their own way, have taken our little slice of [i]Half-Life[/i] to places we didn’t dare dream of when we set out. So, to them, thank you.

And of course, thank you, all of you—there’s no comic without readers, and we’re so grateful for your time and interest.

We haven’t planned anything big for this anniversary because we are on the very cusp of completing the remakes. In the coming weeks we'll be pushing them out the door, as well as putting our entire catalog on sale. We’re so excited about the remakes and can’t wait to get ‘em in your hands. It’s something like 80+ pages, by far our biggest ever release.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/c8f1d971c02f76cb442805ac650c4d0207d0a18d.png[/img]

That release will be accompanied by a new website and a new app, both of which were designed to be sleeker and more accessible. The site’s done with the app close to following suit. Here's a preview of the new landing page of the app.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/f948c1d4c27ac9dd6279eaae5440b95d5dac16e3.png[/img]

Additionally, we’ve added several pages to our interludes. We call them 'bookends'. It’s something we’ve wanted to do for awhile, but it made sense to wait until the big release. They’re a bit experimental, form-wise. Here, for instance, is a piece of text from [i]Interlude 1: The Vortessence[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/caa456024bdcda328e53be362bf92748b7e53383.png[/img]

I know it must seem like we’ve been working away at these remakes for the best part of forever. And it’s true: we have. But it’s equally true that 2020 has been a trying and difficult year, and it’s delayed our plans somewhat. I think that’s true of everyone on the planet.

We are hoping for a better, brighter 2021. If we’re lucky we won’t [i]just[/i] be releasing [i]Chapter 7[/i] next year. But we’ll see. We’ll see…

Mike and Ross

notes.title: Quick Technical Update
notes.notes:
Hey gang,

I just wanted to give a quick update on a couple tech things that have come up within the last few days!

As you may have seen already, MacOS Catalina has come out and [url=https://support.steampowered.com/kb_article.php?ref=1055-ISJM-8568]dropped support[/url] for 32-bit mac applications. There are also some other changes under the hood where apps require Signing, now, which is why [i]A Place in the West[/i] is currently listed as incompatible with Catalina - we have a 64-bit mac build, just not the signing.

I updated my mac to start testing my fix for this, and in doing so, unexpectedly ruined my ability to build the application for [i]other[/i] operating systems. Our current build process uses [url=https://www.winehq.org/]Wine[/url] to create the executables for Windows and Linux, and Wine - as a 32-bit program - is not compatible with Catalina. And, of course, this came up at the same time as a bug where one of the achievements is not accessible.

SO, here's the plan.

1. I'm going to set up a different mac with the ability to compile the app, and get out a fix for the achievement, ideally on Saturday.
2. Once that is dealt with, I am going to fast-track an app rewrite that I've been planning for a while. The bulk of what we have I wrote 3 years ago(!) and I can make improvements across the board.
3. Once [i]that[/i] is all resolved, I'll turn my attention back to a proper fix for Catalina. 

I would like to also take this opportunity to remind everyone that [i]A Place in the West[/i] installs do come with the PDFs for each chapter in your Steam Apps / A Place in the West directory. 

If you are someone who uses Catalina and are outraged at this process of events, please do let me know! I am not sure how many people have actually upgraded. And please feel free to reach out if you have any questions, and I very much appreciate your patience during this time.

Best,

Michael

notes.title: Our Third Year Anniversary...
notes.notes:
We hope you all enjoyed [i]Chapter 6: The Prisoner[/i].

Monday marks our third anniversary of being on Steam! We’ve come a very long way since we initially launched [i]A Place in the West[/i] and we’re proud of what we’ve produced, and more than that, incredibly grateful to all of you who have stuck by us and followed us on this journey. We’re here because of you, and that means so very much to us.

We have been very quiet this summer regarding what is coming next for us, and I imagine many of you are expecting the next interlude, or even some indication of when you might see [i]Chapter 7: The Dark Between The Stars[/i]. We wish we had dates to give you for those, but we have some rather different news. I’ll just get this out of the way:

We’re remaking [i]Chapter 1: Following Portents[/i] and [i]Chapter 2: A Very Modern Major-General[/i]. And with those remakes, introducing new interludes for them: 1.5 and 2.5, respectively.

We understand that may not be the news you wanted to hear, but it’s something we’ve wanted to do for over two years now. We consider it to be of paramount importance that we remake them now rather than later. For a comprehensive explanation as to the whys and wherefores, I humbly point you in the direction of the [url=https://a-place-in-the-west.ghost.io/now-youre-john-hammond/]latest blog post[/url], where Ross has gone very in depth on a lot of our feelings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/481ad1f0d72e1c397d7ec45115c52e0a0cdd8309.png[/img]

The short version is simply this: The first two chapters are something we wrote 6 years ago, and were the first thing we ever wrote and produced. We’re hugely grateful to the efforts of Heath Heil and Rachel Deering for bringing our vision to life, but the writing and composition of those chapters no longer represents the quality we’ve come to expect from our work. 

And I know you might be thinking, “Won’t you feel the same way about 3-5 in a few years?” And, well, no. There are always going to be things we want to improve upon and change, it’s true, but Chapters 1 and 2 fall far beyond what we find acceptable. Chapter 3 is when we began to hit our stride, to settle into our world and characters, (both tonally and thematically) and to really get a handle on things like dialogue and pacing. As we get further in, the alienation and disconnection from Chapters 1 and 2 to everything else is only growing wider, and we can’t ignore it any more. You all deserve better, and so do feature readers.

The new chapters & interludes, totaling some 80 pages, will be released in the Spring of 2020. The first chapter and both interludes will continue to be free. As for Chapter 2, if you have already bought it, you’ll get the remake for free. If you haven’t bought it yet, you’ll still get both. The older versions of Chapters 1 and 2 and [i]The Charnel House[/i] interlude will all continue to be available in the app, under the “Extras” section. We obviously don’t want to take them away from people who have read them, and believe that there is probably some educational value. I expect some of you will find it interesting to compare them side by side.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26319859/75597e331dbc8d51f66c1aaca870fbe0a551d171.png[/img]

To give you a sense of what we’re aiming to accomplish with the remade chapters, we’re releasing a new prologue today! It’s ten pages in length (as compared to the original, which is only three pages!) and is designed to better introduce readers unfamiliar with Half-Life to Valve’s world. It comes courtesy of the amazingly talented Kristian Rossi, Ester Salguero, and Javier Puga. It’s free. It’ll be in your Steam directory. It’s on the app. Or you can just go read it and download it [url=https://a-place-in-the-west.ghost.io/prologue]here[/url]. Your call.

But whatever format you choose, do let us know what you think. We’re always aiming to be as transparent as possible about production, and your feedback is essential. It helps us to improve and hopefully make better comics for you to enjoy. 

On that note, we apologise for not having spoken about this sooner. It’s not always easy to know what the right balance is between “making the thing” and “talking about making the thing”. But we know this will likely come with some push back. After all, we’re taking nearly a year out to remake chapters you’ve already seen, delaying the continuation of the story for some time. We know it’s something you might not all be interested in, and that’s why we wanted to wait until we had more things ready, such as the blog post, such as the prologue. We want you to be able to see the difference, and hear why we think it is important. We are incredibly excited by this, and hope you’ll be on board for it. 

We’ll be listening very closely to what you all have to say, but we also hope you can trust us to do the best thing for [i]A Place in the West[/i]. We’re all feeling really energized by the new scripts for 1 and 2, and we’ll be sharing as much of the production process with you as we can (hopefully more than we have done in the past). We hope that when you do finally get your hands on these chapters, you’ll feel like we do:

That this is the best thing for the story. That it strengthens the narrative we’ve constructed. That it adds to, rather than detracts, from what comes after it. And that it does these characters we have become so very fond of justice. That we’re creating the story they deserve.

Thanks for reading – in every sense.

Mike and Ross

There’s also a new Extra involving [i]“Containment”[/i], for which we give thanks to Rikki "Marphy Black" D'Angelo, that I’ll let you explore for yourself… “Containment” and the Chapter 5 Russian translation are both available in PDF form as well. Finally, we’re releasing [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/980550/HalfLife_A_Place_in_the_West_Soundtrack_Vol_2]Volume 2[/url] of our soundtrack today, with 9 new tracks from Chris Jolley! 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/de101bfda39daf522292488ddf495f952366f512.png[/img]

[h1]Celebrating [i]Half-Life[/i][/h1]
This past weekend we did a Twitch Stream, where Ross played through [i]Half-Life[/i] and we laughed at how many times he died (it was a LOT). If you didn’t catch it and are interested, it’s still available on Twitch until it expires -  http://twitch.tv/halflifecomic. I will also be uploading the original to our YouTube channel, as well as cutting together a shorter “Highlights” reel for someone who wants to laugh at Ross’s deaths, and hear us talk about the comic, but not sit through 6 hours of gameplay. 

We’re talking about going through [i]Opposing Force[/i] and [i]Blue Shift[/i] next, followed by [i]Half-Life 2[/i] and both of its Episodes, so if this is something that you like or would like to see more of, please do let us know! And thank you to everyone who came to hang out and chat, it was a lot of fun. 

Speaking of celebrating [i]Half-Life[/i], Digg.com did a write-up about the 20th Anniversary, and Ross and I both talked a bit about our experiences with the franchise. You can read that here - http://digg.com/2018/half-life-20th-anniversary

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/1ad6a1a20873125f63f778854d59e30c7d4b991f.jpg[/img]

So many things. 

Since it’s the end of the year and we haven’t been as transparent during the course of it as I’d have liked us to have been, let’s take full stock, shall we?

[list]
[*] Chapter 6 is going into Production in December! We weren’t able to produce nearly as much this year as I would have liked because of financial reasons, and it’s great to be getting back to it. My hope is that we can have multiple chapters release next year.

[*] We’ve also been working on getting everything down on paper. Often when we’re producing, we have the next chapter or two written, but now we’re extending our lens further. Ross has been hard at work over the last few months forging ahead into the later chapters. As production is approaching the story’s halfway point(!), we’re spending a lot of time looking at wrapping up threads and character arcs. Currently we have up through Chapter 11 written (at least as rough drafts), with the plan being to finish the remaining chapters by the end of the year. 

[*] Over the next month, I have some homework to do myself: I’m going to rewrite the APW App to try and solve the Windows 10 problems that have been plaguing us for quite some time. I’m also going to be getting back into the world of video editing - cutting the Stream Highlights video together for YouTube and getting back into making the Commentary Tracks. We have commentary audio for Chapters 2, 3, and 4 recorded, and the audio mixing for all of them nearly done, I just need to finish the videos themselves (and add subtitles, which was a popular request with the last Commentary video).

[*] Finally, Translations! These are something that I really dropped the ball on this year. We have translations for Chapter 2 that have been sitting around (largely due to financial strains) so the plan will be to get those lettered and shipped out, and then to do more prep with the published chapters and try to get the translators to help us out some more. I don’t want to make any promises about how much will or won’t be done, but I am going to make it much more of a priority than I have so far. Stay tuned for hearing more about that in early 2019.
[/list]

As ever, making [i]Half-Life: A Place in the West[/i] is an experience that we are endlessly grateful for, and wish to say thank you to everyone who has been with us on the journey so far, and to everyone new who is joining us along the way. I am so excited to share with you all of the exciting things we have in store for the next year.

notes.title: Chapter #4 - "A Spy in the House of Long" Released!
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/f6d24ffa05f5f8780f8e43b3d6846f8cca9a09a6.png[/img]

Hey gang,

We're very excited to announce the release of [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/744920/HalfLife_A_Place_in_the_West__Chapter_4/]Chapter 4[/url] of our fan-made [i]Half-Life[/i] comic, [i]A Place in the West[/i]. Once again coming in at a total of 30 pages, Chapter 4 – titled [i]A Spy in the House of Long[/i] – picks up immediately after the events of the third chapter. The fallout from the Pit disaster spreads throughout the city, bringing its competing factions into conflict. Fearing a loss of power, Governor Moore acts to quell Sejal Rajani's Opposition - a group of dissenters with a radical plan for the city's future - forcing Major-General Long to resort to extreme measures to reassert control.

Chapter 4 was created by the same art team that delivered [i]The Pit[/i] – Kristian Rossi (pencils), Ivan Miranda (inks), Ester Salguero (colours) and Javier Puga (letters) – and features some of the most visually arresting scenes from the comic so far. We couldn't be happier with the finished product, and we're convinced it's the best yet. 

Hopefully you will, too.

[h1]What's next?[/h1]

The script for Chapter 5 – titled [i]The Eyes of the People[/i] – has been completed and is undergoing a few final adjustments before going into production early next year. It marks the end of the present, 3-chapter arc ("Masquerade" as we call it), and brings some of the current storylines to what we hope is a pretty dramatic conclusion!

Of course, before you get to see that we'll be delivering the third interlude (small, 3-5 page shorts released for free) somewhere within January/February. We're really eager to get this one into your hands – it's similarly cosmic in setting as [i]Nal Sidian[/i] was, but unlike that piece of Dreyfus' backstory, it really gets the narrative's wheels moving, and delivers something of a game-changer. More on that (and [i]other things[/i]) in the new year...

In the meantime, please do enjoy Chapter 4, and, as ever, let us know what you think!

Ross and Mike

notes.title: Chapter 4 Coming Soon!
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/3c7721e38c4f319ea7f10dffb5fb2af01517471f.png[/img]

Hi all,

Chapter 4 was intended to be released today, and we’re unfortunately having to push that back to another day (to be determined) because of some poor planning on our part. Because of how we’ve handled delays in the past, I want to get out in front of this one and explain a bit about the process, and what we’ll be doing to fix it going forward.

As you may or may not know, any time a new Store page is created (even for DLC), it goes through Valve for approval (as do pricing proposals). With what we believe to be the combination of Steam continuing to grow at a rapid pace, and the approaching holidays, our new store page hasn’t yet been approved. Ordinarily this process does not take long, and we were ill-prepared for a delay with it.

We typically leave a few weeks gap between finishing the latest chapter and releasing it. This allows us to do several read-throughs of the issue for last minute changes, finish the Steam images, wrap up the store page, ensure that the app is set up to include the new chapter / is stable, and (ideally), have the translations at least for Russian already started. 

In this case, we committed to a date early (trying to coincide with the Half-Life / Half-Life 2 anniversaries), and were very late with making last minute changes. Our timetable as a whole suffered for it and we were later than we should have been getting the Store page to Valve. Going forward, our plan will be to prioritise the assets for the store page assets and move to get that through approval before we announce any kind of date. 

While we wait for that approval, we’ll be shipping an update to the app today that gives a short preview for Chapter 4, and we will keep you updated on a new release date as soon as the new page is approved. Our sincere apologies for dropping the ball on this, but trust us, it’ll be worth the few extra days wait!

notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/78f6befa906194904a7741423723debda36ae934.png[/img]

Hey all!

Today marks the one year anniversary of our initial release on Steam! 

To celebrate it, we’ve released a brand new interlude - formerly known as “shorts” - for free! Titled [i]Nal Sidian[/i], this five-page story delves into the vortigaunt Dreyfus’ past, and explores his relationship to the nefarious Combine. Our plan is to release a free interlude between every chapter going forward. Now integrated into the app’s chapter selection menu, these pieces are very much fundamental to the complete story.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/038ccb15357932257b5ff47bba095d082b3811ff.jpg[/img]

Speaking of the app, this update also introduces some much needed tweaks and updates! We now have improved language support, and we’ve released Chapter 1 and the first interlude ([i]The Charnel House[/i]) for the new languages as well! notes.title: Chapter #3: “The Pit” Released!
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/ae6e99f1d2883ce8debd57c77cd88310a2b4c7c8.jpg[/img]

Hi everyone!

Chapter 3 of the fan-made comic [i]Half-Life: A Place in the West[/i] is now available! Titled “The Pit”, this chapter comes in at 30 pages. The Pit picks up where Chapter 2 left off: Leyla Poirier and Albert Kempinski go their separate ways after an intense dispute, but are both drawn to a gladiatorial arena in New Franklin. Known as “Kal’s Pit”, this seedy arena puts on a show of blood sport against captured aliens from beyond the city’s walls. But when an accident throws everyone into danger, an unlikely hero emerges… And back at City Hall, Major-General Long makes a discovery that will change New Franklin forever.

We’ve made some changes in our team with this issue - Ivan, Ester, and Javier have continued on from Chapter 2 in the roles of Inker, Colourist, and Letterer, respectively, but our previous penciler, Heath, has had to step down due to family commitments - we will miss him, and are incredibly grateful for the wonderful work he did on Chapters 1 and 2. In his place, we’ve brought on Kristian Rossi, who has worked on such comics as Trespasser, The Temporal, and Moonshine. Kristian brings his own style, and we think you’ll love the new direction. As always, let us know your thoughts!

[h1]What’s Next?[/h1]

Sometime Soon (tm) we’ll be doing another application update. This will come before the release of Chapter 4, and will contain another (free!) short interlude between chapters, as well as application improvements including controller support, integration with our soundtrack, and possibly the fabled addition of opting into a two-page layout. This will also include the behind the scenes commentary video for Chapter 2, which I am still cutting together.

We also should be shipping the first batch of our additional translations at that time! As well as the translation of Chapter 3 into Russian, which is unfortunately not yet ready for release today. (Obviously if that’s ready before the release, we’ll do our best to get it out ahead of time!)

We’re also working hard on Chapter 4, which will be going into production the first week of August, and an intended release this autumn. More coming on that soon. 

[h1]What else is going on?[/h1]

To plug some other things, Ross and I have been writing Blog posts on the new A Place in the West website, on topics from artistic style, comics on Steam, and why we decided to use the Half-Life IP. You can check those out at [url=http://a-place-in-the-west.ghost.io/]http://a-place-in-the-west.ghost.io/[/url]. Our website also contains a newsletter signup if you want more frequent updates that we generally post here on Steam. The newsletter comes out once a month and contains some additional behind-the-scenes looks and early teases.

Ross and I were also interviewed for the [url=https://www.ghostcitycomics.com/podcas]Ghost City Comics podcast[/url] which should be released early next week. Be sure to check them out! Their podcast is very informative and, if you are (or want to be) a comic creator, they are doing a competition which can get you feedback, reviews, and even a cash prize.

As ever, we thank you for continued interest and support of the comic, and hope you’re looking forward to sticking with us through the Pit and beyond!

notes.title: Expansion in the West
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/a74e6f13876d8ca55f10a567e6877e2ed297ad68.png[/img]

Hey everyone,

We hope that you’ve enjoyed Issue 2! We're very excited to announce that as part of the build being released on Monday, we'll have the Russian translations for Issue 2 available! We also want to take this time to share some more updates on our end, most notably about Issue 3 progress. But first, some extra things we’ve been working on...

[h1]New Website[/h1]
I’ve redesigned our website to be considerably more than a landing page. We’re going to start using it to open up our production process in the form of blog posts. These will be on everything from creating comics, to the Half-Life universe itself, to the nature of storytelling, and anything else we feel like. Perhaps even topics suggested by readers! We’re launching with 3: “Why a Half-Life Comic”, “On Hiring and Style”, and "A New Kind of Protagonist". We'll be writing and posting more over time, so let us know what you think of them!

Additionally, the website has a newsletter that you can sign up for if you’d like more regular updates from us. The newsletter will be sort of an added bonus for those interested. It is not quite the frequent and small updates of twitter and not quite the large announcements of the Steam page. The idea is to release one every month that goes more into detail about how things are progressing, as well as what things Ross and I are reading or watching to draw inspiration from. It may include behind the scenes looks as well! 

If you’re interested, you can see our blog posts and sign up for the newsletter at [url=http://www.aplaceinthewest.net/]http://www.aplaceinthewest.net/[/url]. 

[h1]Soundtrack[/h1]
Also launching on Monday will be an official [i]A Place in the West[/i] soundtrack. This DLC will feature 6 tracks created specifically for us by Chris Jolley. He’s the only person aside from Ross and myself who knows what’s coming in future issues, and he has used that knowledge to create some very compelling and exciting music. Chris has been doing audio work for us for a while, and created both the Ubdisha sounds and music you can hear in the background of the application. If you like his stuff and want to support him, give it a buy! The soundtrack will cost $2.99. 

[h1]Issue 2 Commentary Track[/h1]
During the second week of May we’ll be recording our Commentary Track for Issue 2! 

If you haven’t checked out the Commentary Track for Issue 1, I’d recommend it. It’s sort of a “Director’s Commentary” from myself and Ross about where [i]A Place in the West[/i] came from, and the creation of Issue 1. It includes a behind the scenes look with some WIP artwork and script pages, and we talk pretty candidly about some of what we did wrong. 

For Issue 2’s commentary we’re doing something a little different, and the entire art team will also be involved! As with Issue 1’s commentary, this will be released as separate and free DLC - an extra for those who are interested in the process.

As part of this, we’ll be doing a Q&A segment, so if you have questions for the team, please do send them our way, either here on the Steam post, on Twitter, or via email. They don’t have to be just directed at myself and Ross - feel free to ask anyone on the art team about their process or inspirations or anything you’d like!

The video itself will take some time to cut together, but I’m hoping to release it sometime in early June.

[h1]Issue 3 Status[/h1]
And now for what you’re most interested in, this week we’re starting with production on Issue 3! In fact, by the time you read this, we’ll have already begun.

Our previous penciler, Heath, has had to step off the project and finding a talented replacement took longer than we’d hoped, but it was worth it. We’re pleased to announce that our new penciler is Kristian Rossi. Kristian has worked in the comics industry for years, as the sole artist on Trespasser and as the colourist on Moonshine, published by Image Comics. We’re incredibly happy to have him joining us, and think you will be, too. 

Issue 3 is still slated to be released in late Summer!

notes.title: Chapter #2: A Very Modern Major-General Released!
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/ddcd0c827c40a59d11e90642570ab87dc0c93b98.png[/img]

Hi everyone,

We are incredibly excited to release the second chapter of the fan-made comic [i]Half-Life: A Place in the West[/i], titled [i]“A Very Modern Major-General”[/i] today as DLC. We sincerely apologise to readers for the unexpected delay last month, but at the 11th hour we were taken by surprise when Valve granted us use of the [i]Half-Life[/i] license. This means that, starting with the second chapter, [i]A Place in the West[/i] will now move into a paid DLC model. 

The hopefully minimal price tag is intended to alleviate our production costs - for further elaboration on this point, do scroll down. We cover it quite extensively! We’d like to thank Valve for the opportunity, and we hope our readers will embrace the change, too.

We have also made the first 5 pages of Chapter #2 available for free as a teaser. The app will automatically update to make those accessible.

[i]"A Very Modern Major-General"[/i] picks up where the first chapter left off - we rejoin Leyla Poirier, Albert Kempinski and the vortigaunt Dreyfus as they enter the strange city of New Franklin. Introducing a host of new characters and fresh intrigues, this chapter comes in at 50 pages and includes 5 new achievements!

The second chapter has been the result of a year of work, and has involved several changes to our team. Our artist from Chapter #1, Heath Heil, has stepped back to focus on raising his daughter. While Heath still did the penciling for chapter #2, he was also joined in this chapter by Ivan Miranda on inking, Ester Salguero on colouring, and Javier Puga for lettering. We also had the pleasure of working with Jiedi Chen and Daniel Gerhard last summer on some additional art which makes its appearance in this chapter. 

So, please, go and read it, and as always, let us know what you think. 

[h1]What are we working on now?[/h1]

I’m continuing to champion our work on translating the comic and working with some very talented people to make the comic available in more languages. Because of the amount we are translating (80+ pages!), we unfortunately don’t have anything to release quite yet, but I can assure you that we’re working on getting these updates prepared. We still have a considerable amount of lettering to do, but my hope is that by early Summer we’ll have at least the following languages released: Brazillian Portuguese, Czech, Turkish, Spanish, and of course the Chapter #2 updates for Russian.

This is not by any means all of the languages we’re working on - we have others which are in varying states of completion. This also does not mean that we are not still looking for more people to help out. Many of the languages we’re hoping to support only have one person working on the translations and it’s very difficult to do since there is both a lot to be done and you don’t have someone to bounce ideas off of or get feedback from. If you’re interested in helping, please do reach out! 

Additionally, I’m still making improvements to our application. I have finished a large rewrite of it that will allow for better language support. You’ll be able to preview this effort in today's update! Simply go to the options menu and select Russian from the new Languages option, and you'll be able to get a taste for how we imagine it working going forward. The other major features that I have lined up for the immediate future are adding the option of using a two-page view, the ability to save your place, controller support, and hopefully finally(!) getting windowed mode to work correctly on Windows. As always, please let me know if you find any issues with the latest build.

Meanwhile, while our artists are on a well-deserved break, Ross is working on writing the script for Chapter #3, which brings us to another announcement…

[h1]Restructuring Chapters[/h1]

Those of you who have listened to the Commentary we made about the creation of Chapter #1 know that we try to be pretty transparent in talking about the mistakes we have made. This process has been a huge learning experience for us, and we continue to learn more and more every day. 

So, with that in mind, let’s talk about another mistake we made.

When we first decided on six chapters, it was before we had even written the script for Chapter #1. We had a rough outline for the overall story, and figured we would flesh out each chapter as we came to it and they’d have varying page lengths. This sounds reasonable in theory, but has also resulted in the situation where we’ve been planning on Chapter #3 to be 80 pages. 

While this is a great chunk of story, the big problems with this are that it means you all would have to wait at least a year to read it, and it also runs the risk of burning out our artists since it becomes a massive project. These are both things that we find unacceptable.

Instead, what we’ve decided to do is retool our idea of Chapters: [i]A Place in the West[/i] will no longer be 6 chapters, but will be “some number of chapters that fit what we’re trying to do”. Each chapter will instead be roughly an equal length (~25-30 pages), and we’ll release multiple chapters per year… like an actual comic. This does not change the amount of content or story, so don’t think we’re just trying to milk it for length - it’s simply a restructuring of how much we release, when we release, and how we approach chapters. 

We want to get more into your hands sooner, and we feel like this is the best way for us to do that. In our prior approach, the plan would be that we’d work on Chapter #3 for all of 2017 and you’d get it sometime Q2 of 2018. Instead, now the plan is that you'd get Chapters #3 and #4 later this year, and Chapter #5 in Q2 of 2018.

Because this leads to some uncertainty as to how many chapters we’ll have, I’ve changed the app slightly to no longer give the names or numbers of future chapters. To give you a rough estimate, it will be something around 13 chapters, with the plan now to release 3 per year, instead of 1 large chapter.

Again, it doesn’t particularly affect the total amount of content, nor the time that the entire run will take, but is primarily a change in distribution.

[h1]Going to paid DLC[/h1]

We know that this decision will be polarizing and we want to talk openly about why we’ve decided to make the comic’s later chapters be paid DLC. The simple reason is, it goes along with having smaller chapters as a way that we can get the comic to you faster. Making comics is expensive - all told, the production of Chapter #2 alone was over $25,000. While this isn’t a big number for a studio, it’s important to remember that this has been funded entirely by Ross and myself from our personal finances. 

This has increased the time we’ve needed to take off between chapters while we build back up our savings before starting production again. With researching in the industry and looking at our own download numbers for Chapter #1, we’ve tried to find a price point where the comic doesn’t feel expensive, yet also gives us the opportunity to be able to speed up production. 

As previously stated, future chapters will be in the 25-30 page ballpark, in keeping with the traditional comic book chapter format. Chapter #2, on the other hand, is 50 pages. Whilst we do think there is a natural break in the second chapter, we have opted not to split it into two to accommodate the new format, and release the full 50 pages. Future chapters will be the same price, but with Chapter #2 there will be more content, which we think is a nice way to introduce you to the DLC model. 

[h1]Finally[/h1]

This is by far the biggest release we've done, considerably larger than our initial launch, and we want to apologise once more for our failures at meeting the announced deadlines or keeping up with communication. 

We do read everything that is posted or emailed to us, even if we don't always reply, and your feedback is instrumental in the future of [i]Half-Life: A Place in the West[/i]. Please do let us know how you feel about the changes, and most importantly, Chapter #2!

notes.title: Update 1.5: The Charnel House
notes.notes:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/742fadbe387a1a948e2e31dfc59b9c3e8c5e67db.png[/img]

We are incredibly pleased to announce the release of Update 1.5, dubbed “The Charnel House”. In addition to containing application updates as the previous updates have, this release marks our first so far that contains additional content since we first launched in late September. We are still on track to release Issue 2 in January, and there will likely be more tweaks to the app in between, but we didn’t want to go for too long without giving you something new and interesting to tide you over. Hopefully this lives up! 

[i]The Charnel House[/i] is a three-page short that focuses on the character of John Moore, taking place a few hours after the events of Issue #1, [i]Following Portents[/i]. Pencilled and inked by Heath Heil, it introduces two new members of our team: Ester Salguero (colourist) and Javier Puga (letterer), so it should nicely bridge Issue #1 and Issue #2!

This update also includes the following:

[h1]New Content[/h1]
[list][*] The Charnel House: A new 3-page short story set in the world of [i]Half-Life: A Place in the West[/i]!
[*] A 2+ hour video commentary about the making of Issue 1, including script excerpts, concept art, and comic pages in various stages of completion (rough sketches, pencils, inks)
[*] We’ve added a new background menu.
[*] Dreyfus’s speech bubbles in Issue 1 have all been changed in both the English and Russian to better reflect his alien nature.[/list]

[h1]New Features[/h1]
[list][*] Six new achievements!
[*] The credits page has been remade, as our team has grown considerably.
[*] The options page now contains a volume setting for the background menus.
[*] The options page now displays all available keyboard shortcuts.
[*] Added more keyboard shortcuts.
[*] The zoom range has been expanded for further exploring the detail of the pages.
[*] Volume and Zoom Settings now save between sessions.
[*] Sounds for clicks and hovers have been added to the main menu.[/list]

[h1]Bug Fixes[/h1]
[list][*] Scrolling via the keyboard is now much smoother.
[*] You should no longer be able to get into a broken state by interrupting animations.
[*] Background audio should now fade correctly.
[*] Resolved issue where arrow keys sometimes didn’t work.[/list]

[h1]Extras[/h1]

We’ve created a Combine font! This font is derived from the typography around the Combine Adviser’s neck.

[url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/e353fb7fef97233f193cb77298ceb90a51935750.png][img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/02f231ee754c689d8205dd4df2e7bfaa5d584e42.png[/img][/url]

You can download the TTF [url=http://www.aplaceinthewest.net/CombineFont.zip]here[/url] and use it for whatever your heart desires. No credit is necessary (since we didn’t design the original language), but we’d love to see what you come up with using it! If you make Half-Life fanart with it, shoot us an email at aplaceinthewest@gmail.com or a twitter mention ([url=http://www.twitter.com/halflifecomic]@halflifecomic[/url]) and we’ll include it in a future update.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/a21bc5cf76ef1aeafe229c3d551f3b3a3eb08acf.png[/img]

[h1]A Quick Note on Virus Warnings[/h1]

Please be aware that we have added a plugin to our application called Greenworks which is what the app uses to connect to Steam (since our app is not written in C++ and cannot access the API directly). We only use this for unlocking achievements. There are some instances where Avast will falsely detect a part of this plugin as containing a virus. This has been [url=https://github.com/greenheartgames/greenworks/issues/66]documented[/url] and is being worked on. 

We wanted to call this out ahead of time because we don’t want anyone getting the idea that there actually is a virus here. If you are in doubt, always take the necessary steps to protect your computer first and foremost. Let me know if this poses an issue for you and I’ll see if we can come up with a workaround in the meantime. I am really hoping to have this resolved before the release of Issue 2. 


[h1]A Quick Note on File Size[/h1]

Adding the video commentary has increased the size of the application. Even compressed, the file comes to about 2gigs. This doesn’t sound like a lot when compared to some AAA release titles, but we’ve wanted to keep the app small and accessible, and it occurs to us that this may be too large for some users who may not be interested in the commentaries specifically - especially when considering that we may have commentaries for each issue! We are investigating some other options for handling this, such as maybe treating it as Free DLC. Please let us know how you feel about the size, content, whether it’s something you want more of, etc.

[h1]Last thing![/h1]

Finally, we benefit enormously from your feedback and do our best to factor it in for future releases so as ever, please do let us known what you think of everything, on either the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/466270/discussions/]Steam discussion board[/url] or via email: aplaceinthewest@gmail.com.

Thank you - and enjoy! We’ll see you again in January for Issue #2.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/61e98a6bf387220b530e293f8c5bd17a5349441b.png[/img]

If you make Half-Life fanart with it, shoot us an email at aplaceinthewest@gmail.com or a twitter mention ([url=http://www.twitter.com/halflifecomic]@halflifecomic[/url]) and we’ll include it in a future update.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26319859/a21bc5cf76ef1aeafe229c3d551f3b3a3eb08acf.png[/img]

[h1]A Quick Note on Virus Warnings[/h1]

Please be aware that we have added a plugin to our application called Greenworks which is what the app uses to connect to Steam (since our app is not written in C++ and cannot access the API directly). We only use this for unlocking achievements. There are some instances where Avast will falsely detect a part of this plugin as containing a virus. This has been [url=https://github.com/greenheartgames/greenworks/issues/66]documented[/url] and is being worked on. 

We wanted to call this out ahead of time because we don’t want anyone getting the idea that there actually is a virus here. If you are in doubt, always take the necessary steps to protect your computer first and foremost. Let me know if this poses an issue for you and I’ll see if we can come up with a workaround in the meantime. I am really hoping to have this resolved before the release of Issue 2. 


[h1]A Quick Note on File Size[/h1]

Adding the video commentary has increased the size of the application. Even compressed, the file comes to about 2gigs. This doesn’t sound like a lot when compared to some AAA release titles, but we’ve wanted to keep the app small and accessible, and it occurs to us that this may be too large for some users who may not be interested in the commentaries specifically - especially when considering that we may have commentaries for each issue! We are investigating some other options for handling this, such as maybe treating it as Free DLC. Please let us know how you feel about the size, content, whether it’s something you want more of, etc.

[h1]Last thing![/h1]

Finally, we benefit enormously from your feedback and do our best to factor it in for future releases so as ever, please do let us known what you think of everything, on either the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/466270/discussions/]Steam discussion board[/url] or via email: aplaceinthewest@gmail.com.

Thank you - and enjoy! We’ll see you again in January for Issue #2.

notes.title: v1.1 Release!
notes.notes:
Hi friends,

Ross and I are getting prepared to leave tomorrow for Steam Dev Days in Seattle, but I wanted to push this update out before we do.

[h1]Changelog[/h1]

- BUG: Fixes a bug that occurs on some Macs where the menu is unusable.

- FEATURE: Adds the option of using Windowed Mode, as requested. Note that Windowed Mode may add some complications as far as browsing goes. It's far from perfect, and I'll be continuing to update it. 

[h1]Known Issues[/h1]

The biggest outstanding issue is that there is still a problem that occurs on some instances of Windows where the game launches to a white screen. I have added a [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/466270/discussions/0/350544272218418731/]Discussion Thread[/url] which contains a workaround. Please report any new issues there that you find.

[h1]The Future[/h1]

When Ross and I return from Seattle, I'll be diving back into trying to fix that Windows bug. I'll also be editing our audio track for the commentary and adding some fancy video to it, so that ought to be released in the next few weeks. We also have had some requests for more features on the app, which I'll be looking at adding (such as Controller support, maybe Achievements, some other things).

We also continue to be hard at work on the comic, continuing with production on Issue 2 as well as writing Issue 3.
